svg.title: Where an Amlodipine Dollar Goes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-generic-spread-funnel; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: Where an Amlodipine Dollar Goes; subtitle: Generic Norvasc priced off AWP versus what the drug actually costs; caption: An AWP-discount contract bills the plan 48 cents for a generic the pharmacy acquires for 1.9 cents, so the plan pays almost exactly 25 times acquisition cost.; assumptions note: Single-drug walk-through as presented by the practitioner. The PBM and pharmacy margins are each stated as about 23 cents and are rounded.; note: Source is Dr. Eric Bricker, AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained (0XFk1m3yGuY at 00.03.09).; stages: label: Average Wholesale Price Benchmark; value: 2.38; display: $2.38; conversion: Starting list benchmark; detail: AWP for amlodipine used as the pricing base in the PBM contract.; label: Billed to Plan at 20% of AWP; value: 0.48; display: $0.48; conversion: 20% of AWP; detail: The percentage-off-AWP discount looks steep yet hides the real gap.; label: PBM Retained Spread; value: 0.23; display: ~$0.23; conversion: About half of the billed amount; detail: The PBM profits about 23 cents on the fill.; label: Pharmacy Retained Margin; value: 0.23; display: ~$0.23; conversion: About half of the billed amount; detail: The pharmacy also profits about 23 cents on the fill.; label: Pharmacy Acquisition Cost; value: 0.019; display: $0.019; conversion: Plan paid ~25x this cost; detail: The pharmacy acquires the drug for 1.9 cents.
